Article Title: Oil prices jump 3% as US-Iran conflict intensifies, Brent crude tops $90 per barrel
Article Text: Oil prices rallied on Monday after conflict between the United States and Iran intensified, raising fresh concerns over crude supplies from the Middle East as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz came under increasing pressure.Brent crude climbed above $90 a barrel, rising 2.30% to $90.13, while US benchmark WTI crude gained 2.07% to $84.20. The move extended last week's sharp rally, when Brent surged 15.9%, its biggest weekly gain since April and WTI rose 15.5%, its strongest weekly advance since early March.The latest gains followed another night of US military action against Iran. The US launched strikes for the ninth consecutive night, while Iran continued attacks across the region, with Bahrain and Kuwait reporting fresh missile and drone strikes.The growing hostilities have also disrupted movement through the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime route that normally carries around one-fifth of global oil trade.The US said that it was enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports, while Iran has maintained that it is targeting ships that violate its navigation rules in the strategic waterway.Shipping activity through the strait has already slowed. LSEG data showed only four vessels passed through the route on Sunday, compared with eight a day earlier.Since Friday, three oil products tankers and one Very Large Crude Carrier have entered the strait to load crude.Adding to concerns, a vessel reportedly caught fire near Oman's coastline. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported the incident northwest of Kumzar and said the cause of the blaze was not immediately known. The British military also confirmed that a ship was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz.The US military has been urging commercial vessels to follow a route closer to Oman while transiting the strait. Iran, however, has responded by attacking ships using that route, insisting it should control navigation through the waterway."The coming days and weeks will provide a clearer picture of the sustainable level of oil exports from the region under renewed dual blockades," Barclays analyst Amarpreet Singh said in a note cited by Reuters."As things stand, we think oil markets are still too complacent about the potential fallout for inventories, which, unlike at the beginning of the war, are at the tightest of the past five years."Meanwhile, military conflict also widened.The US announced another round of strikes after confirming the death of another American service member, who it said was killed in Iraq during the "controlled detonation" of a downed Iranian drone. The military also said "unidentified remains" found on Sunday were being examined after one service member went missing following Friday's attack in Jordan. It said 17 US service members have been killed since the conflict began.In a statement, US Central Command said, "The strikes will continue degrading Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial vessels and civilian mariners transiting the Strait of Hormuz."Iran, meanwhile, continued retaliatory attacks across the region. Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait activated their air defences against incoming drones and missiles, while Israel warned that missiles fired towards Jordan could spill into Israeli territory.On the commodities front, escalating tensions have kept oil prices on an upward trajectory, leaving markets on edge. However, despite the recent rally, crude remains well below the peak of $126 a barrel reached during the early phase of the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude climbs above $90 a barrel, rising 2.30% to $90.13. US benchmark WTI crude gained 2.07% to £84.20. The move extended last week's sharp rally, when Brent surged 15.9%, its biggest weekly gain since April.

Article Title: Hormuz disruptions: India’s crude oil imports from Russia remain near all-time high in July despite no sanctions waiver from US
Article Text:
Russia has strengthened its position as India's largest crude oil supplier. (File PTI photo of Russian oil tanker)



India’s top crude oil suppliers

India’s crude oil imports from Russia continue to be near record highs in July, despite the Donald Trump administration not extending a sanctions waiver. Amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict, Russia has emerged as the key crude oil supplier for India.Some Middle East countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia continue to show supply resilience through alternative routes due to the Strait of Hormuz closure.According to Kpler, a global real-time data and analytics provider, India’s crude oil imports from Russia in July so far have averaged at around 2.45 million barrels per day. This is near the all-time high levels of 2.64 million barrels per day seen in June this year.UAE ranks second with an average supply of 617,000 barrels per day in July so far, and Saudi Arabia is the third largest supplier with India’s average imports from the destination being 586,000 barrels per day in the first few weeks of July.Russia has strengthened its position as India's largest crude oil supplier, with shipments of almost 300 million barrels during the four and a half months since the US-Iran conflict began.Crude sourced from the Middle East through alternative shipping routes continues to account for a significant share of India's imports. Since March, the UAE and Saudi Arabia have ranked as the country's second and third largest suppliers, respectively. Venezuela has also expanded its presence and now features among India's top five crude suppliers.Industry experts say India's crude procurement pattern during the US-Iran conflict reflects a flexible and well-diversified sourcing strategy.Sumit Ritolia, Lead analyst, Modelling and Refining has in the past said: India has arguably been one of the best-positioned major importers, successfully maintaining crude inflows through proactive diversification and procurement strategies.”According to him, import data demonstrates this resilience, with India's crude purchases from alternative suppliers remaining strong despite supply disruptions affecting parts of the Middle East.He added that Indian refiners have effectively secured replacement cargoes while maintaining favourable refinery economics.Before February 2022, Russian oil accounted for barely 2% of India's crude import basket. Between 2023 and 2025, however, it became the country's largest source of crude, contributing roughly one-third of total imports, supported by discounts that at their peak ranged between $15 and $30 per barrel.
Article Summary: India’s crude oil imports from Russia continue to be near record highs in July, despite the Donald Trump administration not extending a sanctions waiver. Some Middle East countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia continue to show supply resilience through alternative routes due to Strait of Hormuz closure.

Article Title: E20 petrol debate: Govt cites data for 23 crore vehicles, says 'no verified evidence' of widespread engine failure
Article Text:
The minister also told the Rajya Sabha that there is currently "no decision" to raise ethanol blending beyond 20 per cent. (ANI photo)

What is Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme?

Amid ongoing debate on E20 petrol, the government on Monday said there is no confirmed evidence linking ethanol-blended petrol (E20) to widespread engine failures or vehicle breakdowns, pointing to both scientific studies and on-road experience from more than 23 crore vehicles across India.Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi said, "More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars, including a large number of older vehicles manufactured before E20 certification, have been operating on these fuels without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending."He further said the shift to E20 fuel has been "phased, calibrated and evidence-based," noting that the ethanol blending rate was gradually raised from 1.53 per cent in 2013-14 to 20 per cent in 2025-26 following "scientific evaluation and stakeholder consultations at every stage."In its written response, the government said every increase in ethanol blending was preceded by detailed studies carried out in consultation with NITI Aayog , the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), the Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP), Oil Marketing Companies and automobile manufacturers.The assessment process included laboratory tests, durability evaluations and field trials examining engine durability, fuel systems, corrosion resistance, drivability, emissions, fuel efficiency and overall vehicle performance.The minister said service records maintained by vehicle manufacturers further reinforce these findings. "One leading four-wheeler manufacturer serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including 1.5 crore older, non-E20-certified vehicles, without reporting any vehicular damage attributable to E20 fuel." Likewise, "one leading two-wheeler manufacturer reported, based on extensive service data, no higher incidence of damage in vehicles operating on E20 compared with earlier fuel blends. "Addressing concerns over fuel economy, the government said mileage is influenced by several factors, including driving conditions, driving behaviour and vehicle maintenance. It added that "any reduction in fuel economy in certain older E10-designed vehicles is generally limited to about 3-5%, while E20 offers a higher octane rating, superior anti-knock characteristics, cleaner combustion and smoother engine operation. "The minister also told the Rajya Sabha that there is currently "no decision" to raise ethanol blending beyond 20 per cent. "Any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including automobile manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies and research institutions," the reply said.The government also clarified that there is "no proposal to mandate the availability of non-blended or lower-blend petrol at select retail outlets," stating that its policy continues to focus on a gradual transition to cleaner and more sustainable fuels under the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme.
Article Summary: The government said there is no confirmed evidence linking ethanol-blended petrol (E20) to widespread engine failures or vehicle breakdowns. Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi said the shift to E20 fuel has been "phased, calibrated and evidence-based" The minister also told the Rajya Sabha that there is currently "no decision" to raise ethanol blending beyond 20%.

Article Title: India's forex boost: RBI's swap scheme raises $20.72 billion so far
Article Text: Reserve Bank of India's special swap facility to attract foreign currency brought in $20.72 billion till July 17, with most of the money coming through Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank), or FCNR(B), deposits.The RBI said on Monday that the concessional swap scheme has seen steady foreign exchange inflows since it was launched on June 8, 2026. It added that FCNR(B) deposits have made up the biggest share of the total inflows.Data released by the RBI showed that FCNR(B) deposits contributed $17.406 billion of the total inflows. Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in $1.97 billion, while External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) accounted for $1.342 billion.The swap facility was announced by the RBI on June 5, 2026, as one of a series of measures aimed at strengthening India's balance of payments and encouraging capital inflows."With a view to strengthening our balance of payments and incentivising capital inflows, the RBI had announced a series of measures, including a facility for offering concessional swaps for fresh FCNR(B) deposits, OFCB and ECB inflows on June 5, 2026," the central bank said.The facility became operational three days later, on June 8. The special window for fresh FCNR(B) deposits will remain open until September 30, 2026, while the concessional swap facility for OFCBs and ECBs will continue until December 31, 2026.The measures were introduced as part of the RBI's efforts to strengthen the country's external sector position and support foreign exchange liquidity amid global market uncertainties.When the scheme was announced, initial estimates suggested it could bring in as much as $70 billion in foreign exchange. However, in recent weeks, some voices have publicly expressed doubts over those projections.Despite the slower-than-expected start, banks remain optimistic that FCNR(B) deposits will see a sharp pick-up before the September 30 deadline for the special scheme.
Article Summary: RBI's special swap facility to attract foreign currency brought in $20.72 billion till July 17. Most of the money came through Foreign Currency Non- Resident (Bank) deposits. FCNR(B) deposits contributed $17.406 billion of the total inflows.

Article Title: Ex-tech execs’ startups find favour with VCs, says report
Article Text:
Representative AI image

MUMBAI: Building for startups as employees can come with their own competitive advantage—young ventures being set up by such tech professionals are finding favour with venture capital (VC) investors who are infusing funds into their companies even though the broader flow of investments continues to be selective.VCs are betting on experience here. The number of such ventures which the industry defines as operator-led startups are very small at this point–some 189 or less than 1% of all tech startups founded between 2023 and 2025 but their share of funding within the ecosystem is growing—it nearly doubled to 11% of total ecosystem funding in 2025 from 5.8% in 2023, faster than that of rest of the players, a joint report released by Tracxn and VC firm RTP Global showed.On an average, operator-led startups also bagged bigger sized cheques and higher valuations for their early seed and series A rounds. “As India’s most disruptive startups like Flipkart, Swiggy, Meesho, Zomato grew, they became training grounds for a generation. Operators have become a founder class. Fewer than one in a hundred companies in this market are operator-led, yet they now land one in ten of its $1 million plus rounds,” said analysts in the report.Operator-founders bring a distinct company-building muscle shaped by experience, scaling teams, navigating constraints and executing through multiple phases of growth, said Nishit Garg, partner, Asia investment team at RTP Global. As AI fundamentally changes how products are built, the qualities that operators bring of execution focus and capital discipline become even more valuable, said Garg.In all, about 50 new operator-led startups got launched in 2025, higher than 37 such firms that started operations a couple of years ago. The broader space contracted with about 2,633 tech startups setting up shops in 2025 from 7,805 companies in 2024.
Article Summary: VCs are betting on experience here. The number of such ventures which the industry defines as operator-led startups are very small at this point. The broader space contracted with about 2,633 tech startups setting up shops in 2025. As AI fundamentally changes how products are built, the qualities that operators bring of execution focus and capital discipline become even more valuable.

Article Title: Hyundai lays groundwork for mass-market EV launch
Article Text:
Hyundai

CHENNAI: Hyundai Motor India (HMIL) is laying the groundwork for its next phase of growth in the EV market, where competition is gradually shifting towards affordable, mass-market models. The company is expanding its charging infrastructure and deepening localisation of components ahead of the launch of its first mass-market electric SUV, slated for this fiscal.The company has so far focused on premium EVs, with the sub-Rs 15 lakh mass-market segment remaining a gap in its India portfolio. Most of its key rivals already have offerings in this segment, with Maruti Suzuki being the latest entrant. Hyundai has sold about 3,000 EVs in India so far this calendar year. The locally developed compact SUV-is slated for launch this fiscal. The launch is expected to precede the implementation of the CAFE III emission norms.
Article Summary: Hyundai Motor India (HMIL) is laying the groundwork for its next phase of growth in the EV market. The company is expanding its charging infrastructure and deepening localisation of components ahead of the launch of its first mass- market electric SUV. The launch is expected to precede the implementation of the CAFE III emission norms.

Article Title: 'Direct violation': Canada vows to protect workers after Trump slaps 50% tariffs on select goods
Article Text: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday said that US President Donald Trump 's decision to impose fresh 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods is a "direct violation" of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA).He further said that the government would continue to support the country's workers, businesses and families. His remarks came after Trump's latest tariffs targeted a range of Canadian exports, including motor vehicles, dairy products and alcoholic beverages, escalating trade tensions between the two neighbouring countries.In a statement posted on X, Carney said the latest US action was part of a series of unilateral trade measures that violated the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA)."This is the latest in a series of unilateral US trade actions that began with the US imposing a series of tariffs in direct violation of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), the free trade agreement between Canada, the United States, and Mexico," he said."These include tariffs on the Canadian auto sector, in violation of CUSMA. Canada, as is its right, has merely matched those measures," Carney added referring to earlier US tariffs on Canada's automobile sector.The Canadian prime minister said the tariffs and repeated threats to Canada's sovereignty had united the country."In response to these measures and threats to Canadian sovereignty, provinces, territories, Canadians from coast to coast to coast have stood together, taking the necessary actions to support our economy and defend our workers, farmers, businesses, and families," he said.Carney said Canada had put forward detailed proposals to resolve the dispute and modernise CUSMA, adding that Ottawa remained open to negotiations."Recognising that the US has been transforming all of its trade relationships, including those covered under CUSMA, over the past 18 months, Canada has made a series of detailed and comprehensive proposals to resolve this dispute and to modernise CUSMA. We stand ready to intensify those discussions in the coming weeks," he said.Reiterating Canada's commitment to open markets, Carney said, "Canada believes in the benefits of free and fair trade, as evidenced by our new government signing more than 20 new economic and security partnerships. This trade dispute has raised costs for families, particularly in the US Canada stands ready to engage intensively to address outstanding issues with the US to the mutual benefit of our citizens."He added, "In all circumstances, Canada will work relentlessly and take any measures necessary to build our strength at home and to support Canadian workers, farmers, businesses, and families."Carney's remarks came after the White House announced a fresh round of 50% tariffs on several Canadian imports, saying the move was in response to what it described as Canada's "discriminatory treatment" of American products, particularly in the automobile, dairy and alcoholic beverage sectors.President Trump signed three proclamations under Section 338 of the Trade Act of 1930, with the tariffs set to take effect 30 days after signing, leaving room for possible negotiations, ANI reported. According to the White House, the new tariffs will apply to most Canadian goods but will exempt energy products, potash, fish and critical minerals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump's decision to impose fresh 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods is a "direct violation" of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the government would continue to support the country's workers, businesses and families.

Article Title: Rupee slips 6 paise against US dollar in early trade
Article Text:
Representative image

Rupee depreciated 6 paise to 96.42 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday pressured by heightened geopolitical tensions, a stronger US dollar and elevated crude oil prices.At the interbank foreign exchange market, the local currency opened at 96.41 and slipped to 96.42, compared with its previous close of 96.36 against the greenback, according to PTI.Forex traders said the rupee remained under pressure as rising geopolitical uncertainty pushed investors towards safe-haven assets, boosting demand for the US dollar. Higher crude oil prices also weighed on the domestic currency by raising concerns over India's import bill.Meanwhile, the dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six major currencies, was trading 0.03% higher at 100.97. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was quoted 0.65% lower at $88.64 per barrel in futures trade.Domestic equities also opened on a weak note. The BSE Sensex fell 58.89 points to 77,649.63, while the NSE Nifty50 declined 22.45 points to 24,216.05 in early trade.Among Sensex stocks, Tech Mahindra, ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank, SBI, Bharti Airtel, Tata Steel, Asian Paints, HCL Tech, TCS, Infosys, Larsen & Toubro and NTPC were among the top gainers, while Eternal, Axis Bank, Maruti, HDFC Bank and Trent were among the major losers.
Article Summary: Rupee depreciated 6 paise to 96.42 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday. Higher crude oil prices also weighed on the domestic currency by raising concerns over India's import bill. BSE Sensex fell 58.89 points to 77,649.63, while the NSE Nifty50 declined 22.45 points to 24,216.05.

Article Title: NSE’s Ahimsa index targets cruelty-free investing
Article Text: MUMBAI: An arm of NSE, the largest stock exchange in India by turnover, has launched an index constituting stocks of companies from among Nifty 500 companies that do not intentionally harm animals while carrying out their regular business. Named Nifty 500 Ahimsa Index, the gauge is aligned with principles of non-violence, the exchange said through a release.“Nifty500 Ahimsa Index will be attractive to investors who wish to invest in stocks of companies that do not engage in activities that harm animals,” NSE Indices said. “The index has been developed in collaboration with the Ahimsagain Foundation as per their Ahimsa Investment Movement (AIM) framework, which evaluates companies based on the extent to which their products, services and business practices align with Ahimsa principles. ”The index could expand investing practices based on the principles of non-violence. “The index is expected to serve as a benchmark for asset managers and facilitate the development of passive investment products, including exchange traded funds (ETFs), index funds and other structured investment solutions,” the release said.Currently at least two mutual fund houses have schemes based on this theme. Quantum mutual fund had launched a fund on this theme in 2024 while last year The Wealth Company MF, one of the newer breed of fund houses, had launched its own scheme.The framework classifies companies into green, orange and red bands. Companies belonging to ‘orange’ and ‘red’ bands are excluded from the index, the release said.Interestingly, none of the bank stocks and Reliance Industries group stocks are included in Nifty 500 Ahimsa index, its fact sheet on NSE Indices site showed. However, all the top software exporters, automobile companies, real estate companies and several from other industries are included in it.According to a release from Ahimsagain Foundation, the AIM’s objective is to redirect ‘capital toward compassion’. According to its brochure, it’s aiming to channelise some of the mutual fund industry’s investments based on the theme of Ahimsa.Total assets managed by India’s mutual fund industry exceed Rs 82 lakh crore, “yet cruelty-free investing remains limited. Many investments indirectly support animal-linked industries,” it said.“Ethical investors lack clear alternatives. (There’s no) simple way to assess portfolios through the lens of animal welfare. (But a) small shift in capital can create a big impact.”
Article Summary: Nifty 500 Ahimsa Index is aligned with principles of non-violence. Index will be attractive to investors who wish to invest in stocks of companies that do not engage in activities that harm animals. None of the bank stocks and Reliance Industries group stocks are included in the index.

Article Title: Stocks, rupee slide as oil spike fuels pressure
Article Text: MUMBAI: Indian markets closed lower on Monday as fluctuating crude prices and global risk-off cues weighed on sentiment, with the sensex falling 443 points or 0.6% to 77,709 and the Nifty declining 96 points or 0.4% to 24,239, while the rupee weakened to 96.45 against the dollar from 96.28.Banking stocks led the decline after mixed earnings, with Axis Bank dropping 5.5%, HDFC Bank falling 5.1% and Kotak Mahindra Bank declining 2%, while Maruti Suzuki India fell 2.2%, as financials exerted the maximum drag on the indices due to their weight and investor reaction to quarterly performance.The rupee came under pressure from rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions, slipping 17 paise and breaching 96.5 in intraday trade, with traders also citing concerns that mobilisation under the FCNR(B) window may take longer than expected. The currency remains close to its record low of 96.96 hit on May 20, 2026, when Brent crude had touched $110 per barrel.“Bank Nifty witnessed selling pressure during Monday’s session as heavyweight private lenders such as HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Bank declined sharply. However, strong buying interest in ICICI Bank, SBI and other PSU banks helped the index recover from lower levels,” said Vatsal Bhuva, analyst at LKP Securities.Crude prices rose to a one-month high during the day, with Brent North Sea briefly crossing $91 per barrel after tensions between the US and Iran raised fears of disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, before easing later in the session. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments said tensions in West Asia are expected to persist in the near term as US military actions expand and global travel advisories for US citizens remain in place.
Article Summary: Indian markets closed lower on Monday as fluctuating crude prices and global risk-off cues weighed on sentiment. The sensex fell 443 points or 0.6% to 77,709 and the Nifty declining 96 points or0.4% to 24,239. Axis Bank dropping 5.5%, HDFC Bank falling 5.1% and Kotak Mahindra Bank declining 2%.

Article Title: At 5% in June, core sector grows fastest in 5 months
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India's expanded core sector grew at the fastest pace in five months to touch 5% in June, compared with 1.1% a year ago, official data with a revised base year 2022-23, released on Monday, showed. The new series expands the core sector basket to nine industries by adding iron ore.The infrastructure industries showed resilience, while output in energy dominant industries remained subdued, reflecting the impact of the prolonged West Asia conflict. The newly added iron ore industry, which has a weight of 4.9% in the new index, grew 43.9%, while output in cement accelerated 9.8%. Electricity generation, however, decelerated during the month but remained resilient with near double-digit expansion (9.8%). Steel output decelerated to 4.6%.Fertiliser production, however, declined 3.3%, its fourth straight month of fall in the wake of West Asia-led disruptions. Other oil related sectors like refinery products (-4.7%), natural gas (-7.4%) and crude oil (-4.2%) too, witnessed continued contraction in production.In first quarter of current fiscal, the core sector grew 3.6%, compared to 1% in the last financial year.
Article Summary: The infrastructure industries showed resilience, while output in energy dominant industries remained subdued. The newly added iron ore industry, which has a weight of 4.9% in the new index, grew 43.9%. Electricity generation, however, decelerated during the month but remained resilient.

Article Title: Monetisation of assets helps NHAI pare debt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Accelerated monetisation of highway assets has enabled the NHAI to prepay loans of over Rs 1.2 lakh crore and repay another Rs 31,300 crore since March 2022, reducing its overall debt to just under Rs 2 lakh crore, according to govt data.NHAI's debt had touched an all-time high of Rs 3.5 lakh crore in 2021-22, raising concerns over its sustainability. Since 2022-23, the highways authority has not been allowed to borrow directly from the market, as it was doing in the past, and instead the Centre has included it as part of its borrowings and shown it as govt capex. As a result, budgetary allocation for the highways sector has risen sharply - from Rs 31,000 crore in 2013-14 to Rs 3.1 lakh crore in the current financial year."We have maintained the accelerated pace of highway construction while continuing to focus on asset monetisation. This strategy will continue, and we are hopeful of reducing the debt burden further. The assets offered by NHAI have assured revenue streams and carry minimal risk for investors. As a result, they have been receiving a strong response," an NHAI official said.Data showed that asset monetisation had hit record high at Rs 41,079 crore in FY24, in the past two years it was in the range of Rs 28,000-29,000 crore.NHAI has set the target to raise around Rs 30,000 crore from monetising NH projects during the current financial year.As per data, NHAI has raised Rs 63,911 crore from monetisation of completed 3,175 km under Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) model since 2018-19 while another Rs 59,588 crore has been generated from placing 2,913 km under the InvIT (Infrastructure Investment Trust).
Article Summary: NHAI's debt had touched an all-time high of Rs 3.5 lakh crore in 2021-22. Since 2022-23, the highways authority has not been allowed to borrow directly from the market. The Centre has included it as part of its borrowings and shown it as govt capex.

Article Title: No move to scrap LTCG tax on equities: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: : Govt on Monday told Parliament that there was no move at the moment to abolish long-term capital gains tax on equities for retail or domestic investors.“The tax policies, including capital gains tax rates, are revised periodically as part of the annual budgetary process and legislative revisions after taking into consideration the macroeconomic parameters,” minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary told the Lok Sabha in response to a question.Investors have been demanding changes in long-term capital gains tax, and the demand gained further traction after the Centre amended the law to attract investments from overseas investors in govt securities. The minister’s statement will put an end to that speculation, at least till the budget exercise begins in Dec.“The tax rate of 12.5% for domestic and retail investors is the same for FPIs for investments in equity... Govt decided to rationalise the tax treatment applicable to investments by FPIs in g-secs by exempting such investments from income tax on any interest or capital gain. This step will align the taxation on g-secs with many comparable jurisdictions,” the minister clarified and added that the move will ensure durable inflows from long-term investors.The Centre had undertaken an overhaul of the capital gains structure in the last few years, bringing all asset classes on a par. Overseas investors have also been demanding changes to the structure for equities, arguing that govt is imposing long-term capital gains tax as well as securities transaction tax, making India uncompetitive compared with several other markets.
Article Summary: The tax rate of 12.5% for domestic and retail investors is the same for FPIs for investments in equity. Overseas investors have also been demanding changes to the structure for equities, arguing that govt is imposing long-term capital gains tax as well as securities transaction tax.

Article Title: Not referring cases to internal ombudsman a concern: RBI
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor Swaminathan J has expressed concern that a significant number of customer grievances that are ultimately resolved in favour of the customer by RBI's integrated ombudsman were never referred to the bank's internal ombudsman in the first place.Highlighting this as a lapse on the part of bank, Swaminathan said that "This is a matter of serious concern because it undermines the very purpose of the internal ombudsman framework". He was speaking at the Internal Ombudsman Conference organised by RBI here last week.The deputy governor told banks that every complaint that must be referred to the internal ombudsman should be referred promptly and without exception. "Complaint management systems should be designed to prevent complaints from inadvertently bypassing the internal ombudsman process due to classification issues or process deficiencies," he said.On the internal ombudsman framework, he said it "presents the institution with an opportunity to correct an error, address an unfair outcome and provide the customer with a meaningful resolution," and added that "if internal ombudsmen perform their role effectively, escalations outside the institution... should naturally decline." He said effectiveness should be judged on different parameters.
Article Summary: RBI deputy governor Swaminathan J expressed concern that a significant number of customer grievances were never referred to the bank's internal ombudsman in the first place. He was speaking at the Internal Ombudsman Conference organised by RBI here last week.

Article Title: IndiGo places over 1,000 engines’ order for A320s
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: IndiGo on Monday placed a record order for over 1,000 engines for its 510 Airbus A320neo family of aircraft. Original equipment manufacturers (OEM) and airlines don’t disclose the deal size as the price is negotiated with the customer, but based on the list price, the cost of the engines is around $14.5 billion. The airline, which currently has a fleet of over 430 planes, has an order book of almost 1,000 aircraft that are to be delivered over a decade. It plans to double its fleet by 2030.The order for LEAP-1A engines at the Farnborough Air Show was placed with CFM International, which will set up an engine maintenance repair overhaul (MRO) in the country.The engine OEMs are going to grow their presence in India, thanks to massive orders from Indian carriers. India is CFM’s third-largest market, with five Indian carriers operating more than 400 LEAP-powered aircraft and have 2,000 engines on order. CFM is a 50/50 joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines. Last Nov, Safran had inaugurated an MRO in Hyderabad.In a statement, IndiGo CEO-designate Willie Walsh said, CFM has been a partner since 2016, and supports IndiGo’s fleet of over 375 Airbus planes.“With a strong installed base, manufacturing in Pune, a broad local supplier network, and advanced engineering in Bengaluru, we remain committed to supporting IndiGo’s growth and expanding our presence in India,” said GE Aerospace chairman & CEO H Lawrence Culp Jr.Separately, Honeywell Aerospace announced that IndiGo has selected its avionics and power systems for its order of 810 new Airbus A320neo aircraft.IndiGo has about 1,000 Airbus aircraft on order, including 60 widebody A350s with an option of 40 more of them. Its June 2023 firm order for 500 A320 family aircraft is the largest single purchase agreement in commercial aviation valued at $50 billion at list price.
Article Summary: IndiGo on Monday placed a record order for over 1,000 engines for its 510 Airbus A320neo family of aircraft. The order for LEAP-1A engines at the Farnborough Air Show was placed with CFM International, which will set up an engine maintenance repair overhaul (MRO) in India.

Article Title: Inflow boost: Foreign deposits, swaps draw $21bn in 40 days
Article Text: MUMBAI: RBI has said $20.7 billion has been raised through its concessional swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, OFCBs and ECBs till July 17, reflecting investor interest after the scheme was announced on June 5 and operationalised from June 8 to boost the balance of payments and attract capital inflows. The collection is almost twice the amount speculated to have been raised. By the end of the swap window, bankers expect mobilisation of about $80 to $85 billion.Of the total mop up, $17.4 billion came from FCNR(B) deposits, $2 billion from OFCBs and $1.3 billion from ECBs. The window will remain open till Sept 30 for FCNR(B) deposits and Dec 31 for OFCB and ECB flows. RBI's out of turn disclosure that about $20 billion has already been raised under the FCNR(B) mop up is seen as a market management and credibility move. The disclosure comes after the rupee came under pressure and inched toward its record low on Monday.On July 18, senior private bank CEOs said FCNR(B) inflows were likely to be below original estimates because of NRI tax treatment, liquidity and regulatory constraints in key markets such as UAE, and operational curbs on Indian banks' representative offices in the Gulf.RBI did not divulge the names of the banks or the jurisdictions from where the deposits have been raised.Bankers said that large sums could have come only through leverage, and that leverage was most likely from tax free jurisdictions such as UAE.Except for RBL Bank, which raised $150 million, none of the private banks have disclosed their collections under the FCNR(B) scheme. Indian Bank MD & CEO Binod Kumar said the bank is targeting about $2 billion in FCNR(B) deposits by end Sept 2026, and that it already has a pipeline of nearly $1 billion to support that goal. However, the actual deposits until last week was $150 million. SBI is understood to be offering leverage to depositors through its GIFT City IBU.Central Bank of India MD & CEO Kalyan Kumar said the bank has mobilised about $8.4 million under the special FCNR(B) window so far and is targeting around $400 million by end Sept 2026. He said that the bank would provide leverage to depositors through its international banking unit at GIFT City.Union Bank of India MD & CEO Asheesh Pandey said the bank has already mobilised around $106 million under the FCNR(B) scheme, and is targeting $1.5-2 billion by Sept 2026 under the special RBI window. He said FCNR(B) is being used to replace wholesale deposits over time and support CASA growth, adding that flows should pick up as awareness improves and customers get more comfortable with rate stability.
Article Summary: The collection is almost twice the amount speculated to have been raised. By the end of the swap window, bankers expect mobilisation of about $80 to $85 billion. Of the total mop up, $17.4 billion came from FCNR(B) deposits and $2 billion from OFCBs.

Article Title: Global urea prices ease in June, still 45% above year-ago level
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: The rise in urea prices moderated last month, though it remained 45% higher than in June 2025. As per govt data, international urea prices were $572 per tonne last compared to $395 a tonne a year back.In a big relief to govt, the urea prices had fallen to $572 per tonne in June, a 40% reduction compared to prices in May. Industry insiders said this was mainly due to a partial lifting of export restrictions by China and fading fears of prolonged war-induced supply disruptions. “India has a comfortable stock of urea for the current kharif season. The rise in prices of sulphur was the maximum at $1,050 per tonne, 265% higher than that of June 2025. Ammonia prices were also 95% higher than last year.Govt data show that domestic urea production in May and June this year was higher compared to the target, offering greater comfort to govt. “We have enough stock to meet the requirement of the current season and more supply has been tied up,” said an official.
Article Summary: International urea prices were $572 per tonne last compared to $395 a tonne a year back. Industry insiders said this was mainly due to a partial lifting of export restrictions by China and fading fears of prolonged war-induced supply disruptions. As per the fertiliser department’s monthly bulletin of June, prices of diammonium phosphate (DAP), potash, phosphoric acid remained higher.

Article Title: El Niño explained: How it can affect India’s monsoon, agriculture and economy
Article Text:
El Niño is more than a climate phenomenon—it has significant economic implications for India. This explainer examines how changes in Pacific Ocean temperatures can influence the southwest monsoon, agricultural output, food inflation, electricity demand and overall economic growth. It also explores the science behind El Niño, its impact on policy decisions, and why it remains an important topic for UPSC aspirants.

The concept in simple terms

How it works

How does El Niño affect India's economy?

1. Agriculture: The first link in the economic chain

2. Inflation: Why food prices rise

3. Power supply and energy costs

4. Government finances

5. Economic growth

6. External trade

Important institutions

India Meteorological Department (IMD) : India's nodal agency for weather forecasting and monsoon predictions.

: India's nodal agency for weather forecasting and monsoon predictions. Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES): Coordinates climate and meteorological research.

Coordinates climate and meteorological research. Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune : Develops climate models and seasonal monsoon forecasts.
